claims.text: Controlled annealing can introduce coherent ordered nanoprecipitates in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
Annealing at 500–700°C for 2–5 hours with a cooling rate of 5°C/min will produce the intended nanoprecipitate-containing state.
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The coherent ordered nanoprecipitates will pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by the nanoprecipitates will enhance mechanical performance.
The coherent ordered nanoprecipitates will reduce grain-boundary mobility.
Reduced grain-boundary mobility will enhance mechanical performance.
The controlled annealing and resulting nanoprecipitates will preserve the magnetic phase transition.
Preservation of the magnetic phase transition will retain a large magnetocaloric effect.
Relative to the as-synthesized baseline, annealing will increase yield strength by 20%.
Relative to the as-synthesized baseline, annealing will increase toughness by 15%.
Relative to the as-synthesized baseline, the magnitude of the entropy change will change by less than 5%.
The proposed effect is not expected to hold for annealing above 800°C or below 400°C, or for times above 10 hours or below 1 hour.
Optimal annealing conditions and resulting microstructure may depend on composition and processing history.
